summary: Mostly no. Squeeze settings, the classic BBW use, did no better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily, and on 1h buying below the 10th percentile did worse. The result that holds up is BBW crossing up through 0.10 on 1h: price moved more after those candles than after random ones at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles, but that comes from when it fires in a window that rose, not from picking direction.

verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h and 4h. On 1h it did worse than random in uptrends and showed nothing in downtrends.
Worse than random on 1h, holding without its strongest stretch, with SOL driving it. Same as random on 4h and daily.
Worse than random on 1h and same as random on 4h. Daily has too few signals to judge.
Beat random on 1h at every horizon. The reason is that these candles are volatile in a window that rose, not that BBW picks direction. Same as random on 4h and daily.
Beat random on 1h at 10 and 20 candles only, from the same volatility timing. Measured within uptrends and within downtrends, it was the same as random. Same as random on 4h and daily.

notes: Buying while BBW was below 0.02 on 1h gave 34,984 entries in 1,273 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.13% behind random entries, inside the luck band. In uptrends the same squeeze did 0.22% worse than random and held without its strongest stretch. In downtrends it showed nothing. The 10th percentile version did 0.18% worse on 1h, mostly from SOL at 0.4% worse, while ETH matched random.

Going long as BBW crossed up through 0.10 on 1h beat random entries by 0.55% after 20 candles, above a luck band that tops out at 0.32%. It shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles and holds without its strongest stretch. These candles are volatile, and the window rose overall. So the gap reflects price moving more after them, not BBW picking direction. SOL carries most of it at 0.63%, while BTC rests on signals on Jan 13, 2021 and ETH on Jan 2–3, 2021.

The trend split matters for the 0.10 cross. In uptrends it beat random by 0.68% on 1h. In downtrends it was fragile, resting on signals on Jun 18, 2022. On 4h the same cross did 0.82% worse than random in downtrends and 1.17% worse on SOL, so the 1h result does not carry over.

Above its 90th percentile on 1h, BBW beat random by 0.16%, just past a band that tops out at 0.13%. It shows at 10 and 20 candles and fades at 50 and 100. Within uptrends and within downtrends it matched random, and only SOL beat random among the coins. It is the same volatility timing as the 0.10 cross, in a weaker form. On 4h in downtrends it did 1.19% worse, but only because of signals on Nov 5–11, 2022, during the FTX collapse.

Some results rest on too little. The daily cross down through 0.05 gave only 10 entries, under the 30 episodes needed, so it is never judged. On 1h the same cross did 0.18% worse than random and held without its strongest stretch, while on 4h it matched random. The 4h squeeze below 0.02 beat random in downtrends by 1.78%, but only because of signals on Aug 15–18, 2026.

For a long DCA bot, a squeeze below 0.02 or below the 10th percentile adds nothing as a start condition on these pairs, and on 1h the percentile version did worse. That is a reason to leave it out. The 0.10 cross on 1h marks candles after which price moved further, which bears on take profit distance and DCA step more than on direction. Test it as a filter beside a trend condition, and expect it to fail in a falling market, where the 4h cross did worse than random.
